newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assemblyman urges increased muni disclosure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assemblyman urges increased muni disclosure.

text.p: California Assemblyman Jan Goldsmith Thursday urged local governments in the state not to resist the disclosure requirements for municipal securities issuers.

"The best way to approach the disclosure issue is not to fight it, not to try to get around it, but to comply with it," Goldsmith, a member of the California Debt Advisory Commission, said. "It's not that difficult to comply."
Goldsmith addressed his comments to bond professionals and local government officials at a conference on municipal bond disclosure in Berkeley, Calif.
The conference was sponsored by Debt Advisory Commission.

Goldsmith said there are some downsides to the disclosure requirements. He said the disclosure rules may cost local governments and may intimidate some elected officials with concerns of personal liability.
But he added that "I have come away convinced that these are the laws of the United States and must be enforced."

He said, "We cannot have lax oversight in this area. We need to tighten it up. We need local government officials to understand the importance of good oversight and disclosure. I fully support the SEC in doing that."
Goldsmith said improved oversight and disclosure would improve bond ratings and "the willingness of investors to invest in California bonds."
